lead: Friday opened the wiki's corpus with a culture argument and a labor argument: [AI-generated posters don't have to be horrible](../summaries/ccc2fd529c5a.md) topped HN while [a case against writing with AI](../summaries/25cb63e5aa93.md) and [a Microsoft director calling scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history'](../summaries/6a0b69e877a7.md) set the opposing poles. [Anthropic added AGENTS.md support to Claude Code](../summaries/d2dc3484409d.md), and [Trump said he would appoint an AI czar and form an 'AI Force'](../summaries/b56a3536794c.md).

sections.title: Can AI make good art - and should it write for you?
sections.intro: Posters as the test case for taste, two arguments against delegating your words, and a darker framing of the whole economy.

sections.title: The labor and ownership fight
sections.intro: A Microsoft director's 'largest theft of labor' line, surprise at the DOJ's pro-OpenAI brief, and India's software exports climbing anyway.

sections.title: Agents get standards and watchmen
sections.intro: AGENTS.md lands in Claude Code, a compact computer-use model, and Raindrop's bet on monitoring agents for hallucination failures.

sections.title: Safety's outside observers
sections.intro: A tour of METR, Redwood and Apollo as misalignment goes mainstream - and Google's argument that Gemini's hacks were 'apparently' not worth disclosing.

sections.title: Washington and the business wire
sections.intro: An AI czar and an 'AI Force', Anthropic weighing a counterpunch to OpenAI's momentum, and the day's funding notes.
